messages.author: 40c76c6e6aaeefc6
messages.subject: change of behaviour of summarise
parts:
Can I ask the reson behind a change that I noticed in the summarise function with the introduction of dplyr?

I started working on something a while ago, before I decided to try and use dplyr - I like some of the dplyr functions, but I find that if I load the library my older code (of some months ago) doens't work due to some changes in the summarise function.
This line which worked before now gives me this

set.seed(5);
df <- data.frame(id = rep(c("A","B","C","D"),7), y = runif(28,-0.2,0.2),  x = runif(28,1,3))
ddply(.data = df, .variables = "id", summarise, int = lm(y~x)$coef[1])
Error: object 'y' not found

while this worked before.

I know I could do

ff <- function(y,x) lm(y~x)$coef[1]
ddply(.data = df,.variables = "id", summarise, int=ff(y,x))

or

ddply(.data = df,.variables = "id", plyr::summarise, int=lm(y~x)$coef[1])

but this means I would need to change the code of the rest of the project (or not use dplyr in this project).

Cheers

Ilaria

messages.subject: Re: change of behaviour of summarise

messages.author: 40c76c6e6aaeefc6
messages.subject: Re: change of behaviour of summarise
parts:
just went through some online comments and realised not much can be done - as the summarise function are different.

Cheecky solution, define
summarise <- plyr::summarise
and use summarize if the dplyr::summarise is needed.

Thanks (for the reply and for all the good work)! And enjoy useR!

Ilaria
